hypothesis: One shared hierarchical discrete state representation plus a generic context-fitted local transition law can identify and roll out two qualitatively different PDE families without an explicit law identifier, family-specific router, governing equations, or hidden parameter labels.

shared_representation.normalization: single mean/std fitted jointly across both law families

transition_identification.features: same generic 25-dimensional basis for every sequence: full 3x3 neighborhood of both channels (18) plus center monomials u^2, uv, v^2, u^3, u^2v, uv^2, v^3 (7)
transition_identification.fit: for each test sequence independently, ridge least-squares 2x25 local map from the two observed quantized context transitions
transition_identification.rollout: recursive; every predicted frame is requantized through the same shared two-stage RVQ before the next step

frozen_pass_rule: PASS only if every one of the 3 fresh end-to-end replicates has requantized rollout MSE ratio < 1.0 versus raw-state persistence on all seven primary tests. No retry or replacement of a failed or consumed replicate.
execution_rule: Run each replicate exactly once in an independent process and persist its result immediately before starting the next replicate.
claim_limit: A pass would show context-based identification and recursive prediction across two synthetic PDE law families under a single shared discrete representation and a single generic local polynomial feature prior. It would not establish unrestricted law discovery because locality and the degree-3 feature basis are supplied.
